etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Borrowed from Latin renegō, from negō (“to deny”). Possibly influenced by renegotiate. Doublet of renay. See also renegade.
senses: (intransitive) To break a promise or commitment; to go back on one's word. [(often) with on]
(intransitive, card games) To break one's commitment to follow suit when capable.
